claims.claim: MiniMax H3 (Hailuo 3.0) is a single omni-modal transformer generating video with native stereo audio, announced 2026-07-31.
H3-Omni-Transformer is a 33B-parameter dense single-stream transformer, with roughly 13B parameters in AdaLN-related branches that can be skipped for inference-only use.
H3-VisualVAE compresses video with a 16x spatial factor, 4x temporal factor, and 24 latent channels (f16t4d24).
H3-AudioVAE compresses 32kHz audio to a 40Hz latent token rate, processing stereo channels independently.
The open-weight checkpoint's official specs are 4-15 second duration, 24fps, 768px short side by default; 2K resolution requires the separate H3-Regenerate-2K module, which is not open-sourced.
MiniMax had not published a technical report for H3 as of its announcement, stating one would follow "soon."
Official MiniMax pricing for H3 is $0.13/second at 2K, $0.08/second at 768P, and $0.05/second for 768P-to-2K regeneration.
MiniMax H3 ranks #1 on Artificial Analysis's Video Editing (With Audio) leaderboard (Elo 1,131), a lead within the +-5 Elo confidence interval of #2 Gemini Omni Flash (Elo 1,128).
On Artificial Analysis's Text-to-Video leaderboard, H3 ranks #2 overall (Elo 1,237) behind Gemini Omni Flash (1,239), leading only within the open-weights subcategory.
On Artificial Analysis's Image-to-Video leaderboard, H3 is statistically tied for #2/#3 (Elo 1,189) behind Dreamina Seedance 2.0 720p (1,197), with a smaller sample size than its rivals.

Artificial Analysis states it receives no vendor compensation for leaderboard placement and computes rankings from blind crowdsourced pairwise-preference votes via a Bradley-Terry/Elo model, without publishing per-model vote counts.

MiniMax released H3's open weights on Hugging Face on 2026-08-03 under a Community License Agreement naming the EU, UK, Republic of Korea, and USA as "Excluded Territories" requiring separate authorization.
MiniMax's own License Q&A states the exclusion is driven by loss of compliance control once open weights leave its infrastructure, not a named government export-control order.

MiniMax's license Q&A cites EU AI Act enforcement (which began 2026-08-02, one day before the weights posted) and "similar regulatory uncertainties" in the UK and South Korea as its rationale for those three exclusions.

MiniMax's Head of Developer Relations attributed the US exclusion specifically to active Hollywood copyright litigation from Disney, Universal Pictures, and Warner Bros. Discovery, which secondary reporting frames as not export-control or geopolitics.

As of August 2026, MiniMax has been proposed but not formally designated for the US BIS Entity List, alongside DeepSeek and Moonshot; roughly 100 pending Chinese entity designations remain paused under a US-China trade truce.

US export controls under the EAR restrict what US persons/firms may export to China; they carry no mechanism compelling a Chinese company to block US users from downloading its own model weights, weighing against export control as the driver of H3's US exclusion.

MiniMax's prior flagship text model M2.7 (March 2026) departed from the fully permissive MIT license used by M2 and M2.5, switching to a "Modified-MIT" license requiring commercial authorization and drawing community backlash.

EU AI Act Article 50(4) requires disclosure that deepfake image/audio/video content was artificially generated, became enforceable 2026-08-02, and carries penalties up to EUR15M or 3% of global turnover.

South Korea's 2026 Network Law Amendment (passed 170-3) allows punitive damages up to 5x proven losses and fines up to 1 billion won for confirmed deepfake/disinformation content, and drew US State Department criticism as overbroad.
MiniMax's H3 model card describes automated input moderation but no watermarking or content-provenance (e.g. C2PA/SynthID-style) system anywhere in its documentation.

A VPA-Guard study documents "visual prompt attacks" achieving up to 100% attack success on the Wan 2.7 image-to-video model and 74.8% on Veo 3.1; H3 was not itself tested but shares the same instruction-based editing input surface.
MiniMax was founded in December 2021 in Shanghai by former SenseTime researchers led by CEO Yan Junjie.
MiniMax's valuation rose from $2.5B (March 2024) to $4B (July 2025) to roughly $11.5-13.7B at its Hong Kong IPO debut in January 2026.
MiniMax's Hong Kong IPO priced at HK$165/share, raising approximately HK$4.8 billion (~$618M); shares more than doubled on debut.
MiniMax's full-year 2025 revenue reached $79.0M (up 158.9% YoY), with a reported "adjusted" net loss of $250M that conflicts with a separately cited ~$1.87B GAAP/IFRS-style net loss figure.
MiniMax unveiled H3 alongside its M3 flagship LLM at WAIC 2026, which opened in Shanghai on 2026-07-17 and ran through 2026-07-20.

MiniMax's chief video-gen competitors include ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 and Kuaishou's Kling 3.0 (native 15s clips at 4K/60fps with multilingual audio; Kuaishou raised roughly $3B at an ~$18B valuation in July 2026), plus global players Google Veo, OpenAI Sora, Runway, and Luma.

The ComfyUI extension ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context by NikoDemon80 was the first of three related "latent masking" continuation tools, initially released 2026-08-07, followed by ethanfel's ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-Contex-Loop and seitanism's fork.

These tools slice the previous clip's tail directly out of its latent representation with no decode/resize/re-encode, using a "masked_av" mode with a pinned backward-reaching audio window, distinct from ComfyUI's native pixel/waveform-anchored "Add Guide" node.
As of 2026-08-18, GitHub star counts were roughly 625 (NikoDemon80), 255 (ethanfel), and 59 (seitanism), all three showing near-daily commit activity in the prior two weeks.

NikoDemon80's own README states continuation quality is not lossless — audio degrades cumulatively across a chain, the tool was "verified on one machine, one resolution, one sampler," and popular speed-optimization techniques further erode continuity.

The only quantitative "seam quality" measurements found come from the tool author's own in-graph Seam Probe node; no independent third party has re-measured the continuation claim via blind A/B testing against a decode-re-encode baseline.
An independent studio review (Curious Refuge, 2026-08-05) found MiniMax H3 produced weaker motion physics and more visual artifacts than the competing Seedance model in head-to-head testing.

A published paper establishes that linear latent-space masking/blending in diffusion models is mechanistically unable to be pixel-equivalent, producing seam artifacts and color shifts by design — addressing image compositing generally, not H3's video-latent slicing specifically, and predating H3's release by about eight months.

Published research on autoregressive/sliding-window latent video generation (CausVid; 2022 Latent Video Diffusion Models) and joint audio-video latent conditioning (UniAVGen) shows latent-space chaining without pixel decode/re-encode is a known, previously-studied technique pattern applied ad hoc by the community tools to a proprietary architecture.

No independently verifiable identity exists for "AbleJones," the community member credited with the 2026-08-17 demo; AbleJones is not an author on any of the three GitHub continuation tools, and no second source corroborates the specific demo.

Banodoco is an open-source AI-art community with a Discord of roughly 22,900 members, led publicly by Peter O'Malley; its own GitHub tools include Steerable-Motion (974 stars) and archived Dough (509 stars); no disclosed commercial relationship with MiniMax was found.

Other major labs separately pursued unified multimodal generation: Google's Veo 3 (announced 2025-05-20) generates joint video+audio; OpenAI shipped native image generation in GPT-4o in March 2025, roughly ten months after Gemini; Meta's Movie Gen (Oct 2024) is actually two separate models in a two-stage pipeline, not joint generation.

A March 2026 paper found a cascaded two-step "generate video, then condition audio on it" pipeline can still achieve high-fidelity synchronized results, complicating the claim that joint single-model generation is architecturally necessary for good audio-visual sync.
